title: Pay your water bill
fee: No fee for bank transfer; 2.5% for cards
summary: Pay online, by phone, by mail or in person at City Hall.
body:
You can pay your water, wastewater and trash bill online, set up autopay, or pay by phone at (555) 010-4600. You will need your account number from the top of your bill.

Other ways to pay

  • In person: City Hall, 1st floor, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm. There is a drop box by the front door.
  • By mail: City of Juniper Falls Utility Billing, PO Box 4600, Juniper Falls, TX.

Having trouble paying? Ask about a payment plan before your due date.

title: Report a pothole or street problem
summary: Potholes, damaged signs, blocked storm drains and broken sidewalks.
body: Report it online with a photo and a location, or call (555) 010-4200. You get a tracking number and an update when the work is done. Most potholes are filled within three working days.

title: Find your trash and recycling day
summary: Collection days by zone, what goes in which cart, and holiday changes.
body: Trash is collected once a week and recycling every other week, on the same day. See the schedule page for your zone and the holiday calendar.

title: Apply for a building permit
summary: New homes, additions, remodels, roofs, fences, pools and more.
body:
Apply, upload plans, pay fees and book inspections in the permit portal. Small projects such as fences and roof repairs are usually approved within three working days.

What you need

  • A site plan showing where the work will go.
  • Construction drawings for anything structural.
  • The contractor's registration number, if you are using one.

title: Report a water leak or main break
summary: Water running in the street, low pressure or no water. We answer 24 hours a day.
body: Call the 24-hour leak line at (555) 010-4111. If water is coming from your side of the meter, you may need a plumber. Crews will tell you which side the leak is on.

title: Request public records
fee: Usually free; copies may cost a small fee
summary: Ask for city records under the Texas Public Information Act.
body: Anyone can ask for city records. Describe what you are looking for as clearly as you can. The city will respond within ten working days, or tell you if it needs more time or is asking the Attorney General for a ruling.

title: Watch or speak at a council meeting
time_needed: Sign up by 5 pm on meeting day
summary: Agendas, live video and how to sign up for public comment.
body: Every regular council meeting is open to the public, streamed live and archived. To speak during public comment, sign up at the door or online before 5 pm on the day of the meeting. Each speaker has three minutes.

title: Sign up for emergency alerts
summary: Text, email or voice alerts for severe weather, boil-water notices and evacuations.
body: JF Alerts sends warnings about severe weather, flooding, boil-water notices and evacuations to your phone or email. Sign-up is run by the county's alert provider.

title: Request a bulk trash pickup
fee: First two pickups a year are free
summary: Furniture, appliances and large items, picked up from the curb.
body: Book a bulk pickup online or by phone. Put items at the curb by 7 am on your pickup day. Appliances with refrigerant need a tag from a licensed technician.

title: Pay a municipal court fine
fee: Court costs as set by state law
summary: Pay a citation, ask for a payment plan or set a court date.
body: Pay online with your citation number, or call the court clerk at (555) 010-4650. You can also ask for a payment plan, community service or a court date.

title: Start, stop or move water service
summary: Moving in, moving out or moving within the city.
body: Request service at least two working days before you move. You will need ID and your lease or closing documents.

title: Reserve a park pavilion
summary: Pavilions at 12 parks for birthdays, reunions and team events.
body: Check dates and book online through the parks reservation system, or call the recreation center.

title: Get a library card
summary: Free for anyone who lives, works or studies in Juniper Falls.
body: Bring a photo ID and something with your address to any library desk. Cards for children under 13 need a parent or guardian.

title: Find your council district
summary: See which district you live in and who represents you.
body: Juniper Falls has six council districts and a mayor elected at large. Look up your address on the district map at City Hall, or call the City Secretary.

title: Apply for a job with the city
summary: Full-time, part-time and seasonal jobs, from lifeguards to engineers.
body: All city jobs are posted on the careers site. The city offers health insurance, a state retirement plan and paid leave for full-time staff.

title: Report a streetlight outage
summary: Tell us which light is out. The pole number helps.
body: Most streetlights belong to the electric utility; the city reports outages to them on your behalf. Repairs usually take five to ten working days.
